subject: maths
chapter_title: A Peek Beyond the Point: Smaller Units and Decimals

concepts.title: Why Smaller Units: Tenths and Hundredths
concepts.definition: When a unit is too big for a measurement, it is cut into ten equal parts and further hundredths: one tenth is written 0.1 and one hundredth 0.01, so lengths and weights gain the precision the task needs.
concepts.key_idea: Smaller units are fractions of the unit wearing a point: the point opens the door to finer measures.

concepts.title: Decimal Place Value: Reading the Point
concepts.definition: After the point, places continue the place-value story in reverse: tenths, hundredths and thousandths, so a number like 4.38 means 4 units, 3 tenths and 8 hundredths.
concepts.key_idea: The point is a mirror: to its right, each place divides by ten instead of multiplying.

solution_steps.explain: Write the whole units to the left of the point.

concepts.title: Adding and Comparing Decimals
concepts.definition: Decimals are added by lining up the points so that tenths fall under tenths and hundredths under hundredths; to compare decimals, match place values from the left until one digit differs.
concepts.key_idea: Align the point and every place falls in line: comparison and addition both read place by place.
concepts.textbook_ref: gegp103.txt, Addition and comparison of decimals

concepts.title: Decimals in Units of Measurement
concepts.definition: Decimals carry measurements across units: 5 mm is 0.5 cm, 250 g is 0.250 kg, and moving the point converts a measure from one unit to its bigger or smaller neighbour.
concepts.key_idea: Unit conversion moves the point: dividing by ten shifts it left, multiplying shifts it right.
